Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF BANYUWANGI,

Considering : a. that violence against women and children as well as trafficking in persons constitutes an act of degrading human dignity and degree, therefore they need to be provided with adequate services and protection; b. that the level of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children is still high, therefore it is the obligation of the regional government to regulate and serve the interests of the community, in this case women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; c. that in order for the handling of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children to be implemented effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a, b and c, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons. TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF BANYUWANGI,

Considering : a. that violence against women and children as well as trafficking in persons constitutes an act of degrading human dignity and degree, therefore they need to be provided with adequate services and protection; b. that the level of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children is still high, therefore it is the obligation of the regional government to regulate and serve the interests of the community, in this case women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; c. that in order for the handling of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children to be implemented effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a, b and c, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons. TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Article 20
(1) In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and human trafficking, the district government may cooperate with international institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

Article 19
(1) The implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and human trafficking shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions.
(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant SKPD, law enforcement, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
(3) The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 24
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons, the Regency Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities that have been established.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPD implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons for the current year.

Article 17
(1) The integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children who are victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be set forth in planning and budget documents which include the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regional Work Units (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Work Plan and Budget of Regional Work Units (RKA-SKPD) and the RKA of related SKPD.
(2) The preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be harmonized among related Regional Work Units (SKPD).

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

CHAPTER XII
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 29
Every person who commits a criminal act of violence in the form of physical, psychological, or sexual violence, neglect, human trafficking, exploitation or acts that fall under the category of human trafficking, as well as other violence, shall be subject to criminal penalties as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 30
(1) In the event that the P2TP2A institution has not yet been formed, then all implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons, shall be carried out by KPPA.
(2) The P2TP2A institution must be formed no later than 1 (one) year from the enactment of this Regional Regulation.

Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women; 34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency. 37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feelings or thoughts as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

Considering : a. that violence against women and children as well as trafficking in persons constitutes an act of degrading human dignity and degree, therefore they need to be provided with adequate services and protection; b. that the level of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children is still high, therefore it is the obligation of the regional government to regulate and serve the interests of the community, in this case women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; c. that in order for the handling of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children to be implemented effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a, b and c, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Second Part
Objectives

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

(4) In carrying out the implementation as referred to in paragraph (3), the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall coordinate with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant SKPD, law enforcement, community institutions, universities, and civil society.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, dispatch, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency. 17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Sending/Dispatch is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Article 22
(1) Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in Article 21 letter c, in the form of victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, social reintegration, repatriation assistance, or other forms.
(2) Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for women and children victims of violence including victims of trafficking in persons, women and children in conflict-prone and disaster areas, women and child laborers, elderly women, women and children with disabilities, women and children victims of sexual exploitation, women heads of households, and women and children of other vulnerable groups.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 24
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons, the Regency Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities that have been established.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPD implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons for the current year.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including trafficking in persons, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence come from all walks of life and are not related to level of education, occupation, or income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, or any particular ethnic group, ethnicity, or race. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed in and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions against acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.
